title: The sea that turned into a desert 🏜️
subject: desert
description:
Could a sea this big really disappear in one lifetime? 👇

The Aral Sea in Central Asia was the world's fourth-largest lake until Soviet irrigation projects in the 1960s diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers. Today most of its bed is the Aralkum desert, and ships still sit in the sand near Moynaq, Uzbekistan.

Sources: NASA Earth Observatory ("Aral Sea Continues to Shrink", 2009) and NASA Scientific Visualization Studio ("Shrinking Aral Sea"); ESA Earth from Space (Envisat Aral Sea images); ScienceAlert (2025); Caspian Post ("Moynak: Memories of the Aral Sea", 2023)

scenes.text: Fishing ships are rusting in the middle of a desert.
That sand was the floor of the Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake.
In the 1960s, Soviet planners diverted its 2 rivers to water cotton.
Moynaq's cannery once packed 30 tonnes of fish a day. The nearest shore is now about 100 kilometers away.
Each year, storms lift at least 150,000 tonnes of salt and sand off the dry seabed.
Of 68,000 square kilometers of sea, about 8,000 are still water.
